title: The tooth fights back: pulp to periapex
topic: The lines of immune defense from dentin to the periapex, why the lesion contains but cannot reach the canal infection.

claims.claim: Odontoblasts sense bacteria: TLR2, TLR4 (receptors localized in human odontoblasts and their processes)
claims.source: Veerayutthwilai et al., Oral Microbiol Immunol 2007;22:5-13 (PMID 17241164)

claims.claim: Dendritic cells sample; then T cells, macrophages and neutrophils accumulate as caries deepens
claims.source: Farges et al., Mediators Inflamm 2015;2015:230251 (PMID 26538821), review

claims.claim: Necrotic pulp: no immune access, a protected bacterial reservoir
claims.source: Graves et al., J Oral Microbiol 2011;3:5304 (PMID 21547019), review

claims.claim: Periapical lesion cells: macrophages, T and B cells, plasma cells, neutrophils, with antibodies (unranked; schematic)
Plasma cells in periapical granulomas make mostly IgG (81.9% of immunoglobulin-positive plasma cells, 10 human granulomas)
claims.source: Matthews & Mason, Br J Oral Surg 1983;21:192-7 (PMID 6578841)

claims.claim: IL-1, TNF, PGE2 and RANKL switch on osteoclasts; bone resorbs (signals shown side by side; schematic model)
claims.source: Graves et al., J Oral Microbiol 2011;3:5304 (PMID 21547019), review; Wang & Stashenko, J Endod 1993;19:107-11 (PMID 8509747)

claims.claim: The lesion contains the infection but cannot reach the canal; treatment can (it reduces the canal's microbial load)
claims.source: Nair, Crit Rev Oral Biol Med 2004;15:348-81 (PMID 15574679); Márton & Kiss, Oral Microbiol Immunol 2000;15:139-50 (PMID 11154396)

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: sequence largely from rodent models; cell numbers, sizes and timing are illustrative
claims.source: Stashenko et al., J Endod 1992;18:422-6 (PMID 9796508); Graves et al. 2011 (PMID 21547019)

caption:
The tooth fights back, from dentin to apex.

Odontoblasts (TLR2/TLR4) meet bacteria first; dendritic cells, T cells, macrophages, neutrophils follow.
A necrotic canal is out of immune reach: a protected reservoir.
At the apex the lesion holds the line (plasma cells: mostly IgG) at the cost of bone: IL-1, TNF, PGE2, RANKL, osteoclasts.
It contains. It can't reach the canal. Treatment can.

Refs: Veerayutthwilai 2007, Oral Microbiol Immunol; Farges 2015, Mediators Inflamm; Graves 2011, J Oral Microbiol; Stashenko 1992, J Endod; Matthews & Mason 1983, Br J Oral Surg; Nair 2004, Crit Rev Oral Biol Med
Schematic; mostly rodent data.
